title: Hex.pm registry unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-129514, CVSS 10.0) exploited against six hex.pm servers on Nov 23
why: Hex.pm's own incident post (Nov 24) confirms an attacker ran commands on six web servers on Nov 23 via CVE-2026-129514 (GHSA-9pmm-hf4r-27pg); covered by THN and SOCRadar. Not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.25) and no Microsoft advisory or Defender coverage seen.
action: Have Elixir/Erlang developers change hex.pm passwords and reset 2FA, rotate Hex API keys used in CI, fetch only from repo.hex.pm (no mirrors) until the new signed Hex client ships, and review recent releases/ownership changes on your packages.
product: hex.pm package registry service (hexpm Erlang-term request-body parser, pre-fix)

title: GeoServer: attackers probing CVE-2026-129243 OWS auth bypass and CVE-2026-120705 file read, part of a public 5-bug unauthenticated RCE chain
why: watchTowr reported error-based exploit probes (creating/invoking stored queries) against both CVEs after GeoServer's Nov 23 advisories; a Rapid7 researcher published PoC for the 5-bug unauth RCE chain (THN, SecurityWeek). Neither CVE is in CISA KEV (2026.11.25); no Microsoft signal.
action: Upgrade internet-facing GeoServer to 2.27.7 / 2.28.6 / 3.0.2 now, and review logs for anonymous CreateStoredQuery / stored-query WFS requests since Nov 23.

title: GL.iNet GoodCloud cloud-management flaw exploited to plant malware on GL.iNet routers and KVM devices
why: GL.iNet's security notice (issued Nov 20, updated Nov 23) confirms an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its GoodCloud remote-management service to install malware on some routers and KVM devices. BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, SecurityWeek and Cybernews covered it Nov 22-23; Cybernews cites researchers who found malware or older backdoors on 166 of 199 routers they analyzed. There is no CVE, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft signal. KVMs give the attacker a path to the connected computers. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Install the GL.iNet security firmware for each router or KVM model, check devices for the infection indicator in GL.iNet's notice, and, if a KVM was infected, check the computers connected to it.
product: GL.iNet routers and remote KVMs managed through GoodCloud (security firmware per model, e.g. GL-MT3000/MT6000 4.11.1, KVM RM1 1.10.3)

affected.product: GL.iNet GL-AX1800 / AXT1800 / SFT1200 / X3000 / XE3000 firmware
GL.iNet KVM RM1 / RM1V2 / RM10 / RM10RC / RM1PE / RM4PE firmware

title: Xen Orchestra empty-object login token auth bypass (exploited) now tracked as CVE-2026-133469
why: The Xen Orchestra authentication bypass we have tracked since Nov 10 as exploited in the wild (vendor advisory VSA-2026-062, fixed 6.9.2/6.10.1) received CVE-2026-133469 on Nov 23 (NVD 9.8, GitHub advisory GHSA-2r3w-c2vx-fv5g). VulDB and CVEReports describe it as actively exploited. It is not in CISA KEV and there is no Microsoft signal. A Sploitus-listed "PoC" repo is from a publisher previously seen posting simulated labs, so it is not counted as public exploit code. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade Xen Orchestra to 6.9.2 or 6.10.1, revoke all existing authentication tokens, and review XO audit logs for unexpected REST logins.

title: VMware vCenter vmdir unauthenticated authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123903, 9.8): unverified public PoC claimed
why: Broadcom VMSA-2026-0011 (Nov 24) fixes a 9.8 network authentication bypass in vCenter's directory service. On Nov 24 a GitHub repository claiming a working PoC appeared (reported by The Layman Security, Rescana and Mallory; none verified it). No exploitation reported yet, not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.24). Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Patch vCenter to 9.1.2, 9.0.2.0300 or 8.0 U3m (VCF 5.2.5) now, and keep vCenter management interfaces off untrusted networks.
product: VMware vCenter Server 9.1.x, 9.0.x, 8.0, 7.0 (and VCF/vSphere Foundation/Telco Cloud vCenter)

title: HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor/Router unauthenticated root command injection via Salt minion ID (CVE-2026-103406) added to CISA KEV
why: Not ahead: CISA added it to KEV on Nov 25, 2026 (BOD due Nov 28).
action: Upgrade Session Smart Conductors to 7.0.5/7.1.7/7.2.3 and restrict the conductor's Salt/provisioning ports to managed routers only; hunt for unexpected minion IDs.
product: Session Smart Conductor / Session Smart Router before 7.0.5, 7.1.7, 7.2.3

title: Danfoss refrigeration controllers: CVEs assigned for default-credential access (AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800, used in the supermarket sabotage wave) and an unauthenticated CGI overflow (AK-SM 8xxA)
why: Danfoss advisory DSA-2026-12-01 (published Nov 20) assigns CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9) to the factory default credentials on legacy AK-SC 355/AK-SM 800 controllers and CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3) to an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA. Reporting on the European refrigeration-sabotage wave (decryptiondigest, SOCRadar) names default credentials on internet-exposed AK-SM 800A/8xxA as an entry point. Neither new CVE is in CISA KEV. Whether 129713 is one of the six unpatched AK-SM800A flaws disclosed Nov 11 is not confirmed. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Take AK-SC/AK-SM controllers off the internet (VPN only), change the default Supervisor credentials now, and follow DSA-2026-12-01 for AK-SM 8xxA firmware.
product: Danfoss legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800 Series (all versions); AK-SM 8xxA Series

title: Idunno.AntiCsrf deserialization RCE (abandoned ASP.NET library) exploited, now in CISA KEV
why: Not ahead any more: CISA added CVE-2026-131914 to KEV on Nov 24, 2026.
action: Find ASP.NET/IIS apps that reference Idunno.AntiCsrf and remove or replace the library; there is no patch.

title: Rejetto HFS 3.x session forgery to unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-61500): exploited since Oct 1, used by GT13 as a relay, still not in CISA KEV
why: VulnCheck has seen exploitation since Oct 1, and GreyNoise's GT13 report (Nov 23) shows the actor took over an HFS server with CVE-2026-61500 on Oct 2 to use as its relay box. The CISA KEV catalog (version 2026.11.23, checked this run) still does not list it. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade HFS to 3.2.1 or later (or take it offline), then rotate admin credentials and check server_code settings and admin-panel logs for logins you did not make.

title: Malicious npm package @leadstack/crm-connect installs Hermes Agent as a Telegram-controlled backdoor on servers
why: SafeDep (Nov 19, trending on Hacker News Nov 21) documents the package posing as a LeadStack CRM client that, on install, sets up the open-source Hermes Agent as a systemd service steered from the attacker's Telegram bot. No CVE, so it cannot be in CISA KEV; no Microsoft blog or Defender write-up seen. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Search lockfiles, npm caches and CI logs for @leadstack/crm-connect; on any hit, isolate the host, remove the disguised systemd service and rotate credentials it could reach.

title: Radware Cloud WAF: exposed unauthenticated management API leaked customer log-export cloud keys (AWS S3, Azure Blob, SFTP)
why: Radware's root-cause report (via BleepingComputer, Nov 24) says an internal Cloud WAF management API was reachable from the internet without authentication and was accessed on Nov 19, exposing customer contacts and, for some customers, log-export credentials. Some customers saw AWS alerts of an unfamiliar IP probing log buckets. Hosted-service incident: no CVE, no KEV entry, nothing from Microsoft. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: If you export Radware Cloud WAF logs, rotate the S3 keys, Azure Blob keys/SAS tokens and SFTP credentials now and review storage access logs from Nov 19 on.
product: Radware Cloud WAF / AppSec (WAF, Bot) hosted service

title: Rackspace Spot breach: leaked credentials let attackers deploy pods and read customer Kubernetes Secrets; service shutting down Dec 8
why: Rackspace confirmed (BleepingComputer, SC Media) that on Nov 17 attackers used compromised credentials to deploy unauthorized pods and may have read cluster Secrets and storage files; on Nov 24 it announced Spot will be shut down Dec 8. No CVE, not in KEV, no Microsoft coverage. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Rotate every secret that was stored in Rackspace Spot clusters and look for use of those credentials since Nov 17; plan migration before Dec 8.

title: F5 BIG-IP out-of-band hotfixes: five critical unauthenticated TMM stack overflows (APM, iRules) that may allow RCE
why: F5's Nov 18 out-of-band notification (K000164058/K000164239) fixes critical stack overflows that let a remote unauthenticated attacker crash TMM and may allow code execution; BleepingComputer, THN and SecurityWeek cover it. No exploitation reported, not in CISA KEV, nothing from Microsoft. Shadowserver sees 177,000+ exposed BIG-IP and 14,600 APM instances. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Check BIG-IP APM and iRule (including DNS::scrape) usage against F5's K articles and install the out-of-band hotfixes on exposed systems.
product: F5 BIG-IP (APM, iRules configurations, BIG-IP DNS DNS::scrape iRule)

title: Upload2Shell: Ghostscript Type 1 font-loader use-after-free escapes -dSAFER for command execution via uploads, mail and print pipelines
why: -free in Ghostscript's Type 1 font loader that crosses the -dSAFER sandbox and runs attacker-chosen commands as the rendering process. pwn.ai lists confirmed command execution in production or lab paths, including Google's document renderer (since fixed), WordPress Core uploads (separate CVE-2026-65640, fixed Aug 12) and unauthenticated IPP print jobs to Debian 13 CUPS. Artifex fixed it in Ghostscript 10.08.0 (Sep 8). oss-security, The Hacker News and CyberSecurityNews cover it. pwn.ai says per-product PoCs are not yet published, and no exploitation in the wild has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft advisory or Defender guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or your distro's package that fixes CVE-2026-125396, and check that upload, preview and print services do not pass untrusted files to Ghostscript (for example, disable PS/PDF/EPS coders in ImageMagick policy.xml).
product: Ghostscript before 10.08.0 (distro backports vary, e.g. Debian 13 fixed in 10.05.1~dfsg-1+deb13u2); reached through ImageMagick, WordPress Core uploads, CUPS and other renderers

title: VMware ESX I/O filter service unauthenticated network RCE (CVE-2026-123910 / CVE-2026-123911, CVSS 9.8, VMSA-2026-0011)
why: Broadcom VMSA-2026-0011 (Nov 24) fixes two 9.8 flaws (a heap out-of-bounds write and a use-after-free) in the ESX I/O filter service that an attacker with network access to the host can use to run code, with no guest VM access needed. No exploitation has been reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Apply ESXi80U3m-25926933 / ESXi-9.1.2.0 / ESXi-9.0.2.0200, or the KB463535 workaround on 8.0, and limit network access to ESX management interfaces.

title: @fastify/express and @fastify/middie path-scoped middleware bypass: unauthenticated requests skip auth/rate-limit middleware (five CVEs, CVSS 9.1)
why: Fastify published GHSA-w877-hjcp-88rc and NVD added five CVSS 9.1 CVEs on Nov 21. URL decoding and normalisation mismatches between Fastify's router and the Express or middie middleware layer let an unauthenticated request reach a route handler while skipping the path-scoped authentication, authorization or rate-limit middleware meant to protect it. @fastify/express 4.0.10 fixes it. No public PoC or exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade @fastify/express to 4.0.10 and @fastify/middie past 9.3.7, and move auth checks into Fastify hooks (onRequest/preHandler) instead of path-scoped middleware.

title: better-auth phone-number plugin lets attackers claim unverified numbers and take over accounts via phone OTP sign-in
why: VulnCheck assigned CVE-2026-134322 on Nov 21 for a better-auth advisory (GHSA-q747-mqgr-4gh7) fixed in the Nov 3 security release. Sign-up and other flows save phone numbers before they are verified, and phone-OTP sign-in then uses that number to pick the account, so an attacker can attach a victim's number and take over the account (CVSS 4.0 8.6, needs some user interaction). No PoC or exploitation has been reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: If you use better-auth with the phone number plugin, upgrade to 1.7.16 (or 1.8.0-beta.5) and review accounts whose phone numbers were never verified.
product: better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 (phone number plugin)

title: Rclone serve sftp --auth-proxy authentication bypass via cache key that omits credentials
why: NVD published CVE-2026-134352 (CVSS 9.2) on Nov 21. In rclone serve sftp with --auth-proxy, the cache key does not include the authentication material, so a later login can reuse an earlier authenticated session. It only affects that configuration. Fixed in 1.76.0. The only source is the NVD record, with no PoC or exploitation reported. It is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft guidance. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade rclone to 1.76.0 wherever 'rclone serve sftp --auth-proxy' runs, or stop that service until you can.

title: Synology DSM / BeeStation OS OAuth API argument injection: unauthenticated arbitrary file read/write (CVSS 9.8, Synology-SA-26:21)
why: Synology published Synology-SA-26:21 around Nov 19 for CVE-2026-120382 (CVSS 9.8, no authentication or user interaction needed). NVD published it Nov 22, and SOC Prime and DEV Community covered it Nov 21; as of Nov 20 some branches were still marked 'Ongoing' in the advisory. No exploitation or public PoC reported (OffSeq: not known to be exploited, Nov 23). Not in CISA KEV; Microsoft has no signal on it. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Update DSM to the fixed build for your branch; where no build is out yet, deactivate the OAuth Service package and keep DSM off the internet.
product: DiskStation Manager (DSM) 6.2-7.4 before the fixed builds; BeeStation OS 1.5

title: Spring Data Elasticsearch SpEL injection through @Query method arguments (RCE when untrusted input reaches a repository query)
why: Spring published CVE-2026-123886 (High, CVSS 8.8) on Nov 19, and NVD on Nov 23. Untrusted method arguments are evaluated as SpEL inside string-based @Query methods, which can lead to code execution. Fixed in 6.0.9 and 6.1.3. There is no public PoC or exploitation, it is not in CISA KEV, and there is no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade Spring Data Elasticsearch to 6.1.3 or 6.0.9 (the 5.x line is listed as affected through 5.5.13 with no open-source fix named) and find string-based @Query methods that take user input.

title: AutoGPT Platform ships a public default JWT secret: forge admin tokens (CVE-2026-130169, CVSS 10)
why: Disclosed Nov 23 (NVD/CVE, CVSS 10): AutoGPT Platform deployments that keep the hardcoded HS256 key from .env.default accept forged JWTs for any user or admin. VulDB lists AutoGPT 0.8.0 as the upgrade. No exploitation report found; OffSeq lists honeypot/exposure data without detail. Not in CISA KEV, no Microsoft signal. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Rotate the JWT secret in every self-hosted AutoGPT deployment (never use the .env.default value), upgrade past 0.7.4, and invalidate existing sessions.

title: Chrome critical sandbox escape in Variations (CVE-2026-134401) fixed in 158.0.8127.88; Edge fix not yet seen
why: Google shipped Chrome 158.0.8127.88/.89 on Nov 23 for a Critical-rated Variations flaw that lets a crafted HTML page run code outside the sandbox (NVD 9.6). No exploitation reported. Not in CISA KEV, and no Microsoft Edge security release or MSRC entry for this CVE was found as of Nov 24 09Z (the latest Edge security note found covers CVE-2026-125350). Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Force Chrome to 158.0.8127.88+ across the fleet (relaunch required) and watch for the matching Microsoft Edge security update.

title: Joomla 6.2.1 / 5.4.11 fix 58 flaws incl. web installer authentication bypass (CVE-2026-123214) and media field RCE (CVE-2026-129393)
why: Joomla released 6.2.1 and 5.4.11 on Nov 24 with 58 security fixes (4 critical), including missing authentication in the web installer on installed sites (CVSS 9.2) and RCE through media custom field parameters (9.4). No public exploit or attacks reported yet; not in CISA KEV. A very similar Drupal installer flaw was exploited within a day of disclosure last week. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Update Joomla sites to 6.2.1 or 5.4.11 now; Joomla 4 and older sites should be moved to a supported release.

title: IkonRAT: poisoned update of an automotive-industry business app delivers Node.js backdoor and Windows credential theft
why: Blackpoint Cyber (shared via AlienVault OTX, Nov 25) reports a November 2026 supply-chain compromise: 6,438 bytes of malicious JavaScript in a legitimate app's server.bundle.js delivering IkonRAT, with follow-on UAC bypass and Windows credential theft. The affected product is not named in what we saw; no CVE, not in KEV, no Microsoft report. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Use the Blackpoint report's indicators to hunt for node.exe started by line-of-business apps making unexpected outbound connections, especially from automotive-sector software updated in November.
product: Unnamed automotive-industry business application (server.bundle.js document-rendering component)

title: WP Rocket < 3.24.2 unauthenticated path traversal rated 9.8 (Patchstack labels it RCE)
why: Published to NVD Nov 25 via Patchstack (CVSS 9.8, unauthenticated, titled RCE); widely deployed caching plugin. No PoC or ITW yet; not in CISA KEV.
action: Update WP Rocket to 3.24.2 or later on all WordPress sites (premium plugin: confirm the license-based auto-update actually applied).

title: WhatsApp for Android ad-reply URL validation flaw (IP leak) suspected exploited in scam campaigns
why: WhatsApp says it found the bug while disrupting a scam campaign and suspects it was used to make scam messages look credible (The Hacker News, SecurityWeek, Security Affairs, Nov 20). Not in CISA KEV; nothing from Microsoft (not a Microsoft product). Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Push WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business for Android 2.26.17.4 or later on managed Android devices.
product: WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business for Android before 2.26.17.4

title: simple-git argument injection: --exec bypasses allowUnsafePack guard for command execution (fixed 4.1.0)
why: NVD and a VulnCheck advisory published CVE-2026-134815 on Nov 22 (CVSS 4.0 9.2). The --exec option to ls-remote, archive, fetch-pack or send-pack bypasses simple-git's allowUnsafePack guard. No exploitation or public PoC reported (OffSeq: not known to be exploited). Not in CISA KEV; nothing from Microsoft. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade simple-git to 4.1.0 or later (check transitive dependencies with npm ls simple-git), and never pass user-controlled strings as git options.

title: Erlang/OTP ssl TLS 1.2/DTLS client accepts anonymous handshake: any server can be impersonated (CVE-2026-124286, CVSS 9.1)
why: The EEF CNA published the advisory on Nov 24, and fixed OTP releases are out. The flaw silently disables certificate checks for TLS 1.2/DTLS clients in Erlang/Elixir apps. No exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Upgrade to OTP 27.3.4.14 / 28.5.0.9 / 29.0.3 (or the matching ssl versions); until then restrict clients to TLS 1.3 ({versions, ['tlsv1.3']}).

title: Firefox 161 / ESR 153.8 / ESR 115.46 fix multiple 9.6 sandbox escapes and memory-safety bugs
why: Mozilla advisory MFSA 2026-131 and around 50 NVD records published Nov 24, including several 9.6 sandbox escapes (Graphics/WebRender, Networking, cubeb). No exploitation reported (OffSeq: not known exploited); not in CISA KEV. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Push Firefox 161 / ESR 153.8 / ESR 115.46 and Thunderbird 161 through your software management tooling.

title: Thymeleaf restricted expression mode bypass enables template-injection RCE (CVE-2026-136410, fixed 3.1.6.RELEASE)
why: VulnCheck published CVE-2026-136410 (CVSS 9.5/9.0) on Nov 24 for GHSA-2wmw-5fmc-m25v; Ostorlab describes it as a template-injection RCE path. Not reported exploited, no public exploit seen, not in CISA KEV. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Bump Thymeleaf to 3.1.6.RELEASE (override the Spring Boot managed version if needed) and check templates for user input reaching expressions.

title: GPGME double free via crafted long OpenPGP user ID (affects Gpg4win, mail clients, Samba, Flatpak)
why: GnuPG advisory (Nov 20, forwarded to oss-security) rates it critical: a crafted key can trigger a double free usable to exfiltrate data, RCE not ruled out; disclosed early because of the Ruby2Shell GitLab update. No exploitation or public PoC seen; not in CISA KEV; no Microsoft guidance. Nov 21: oss-security thread notes Red Hat had patched this downstream years ago; still no PoC or exploitation. Nov 24 09Z recheck: still not in CISA KEV (the only KEV additions on Nov 23 were MONAI Label and N-able MailAssure) and no Microsoft advisory. Nov 24 17Z recheck: not in CISA KEV (catalog 2026.11.23) and no new MSRC entries this run. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Update GPGME to 2.3.1 (Gpg4win 5.1.2 on Windows) and rebuild statically linked tools; apply distro updates as they land.

title: Zstandard 1.5.1-1.5.7 decompression leaks up to 64 KiB of earlier-decompressed data/uninitialized memory (CVE-2026-124851)
why: Meta published the advisory and it was posted to oss-security on Nov 24; the ZstdSharp port is still unfixed (GitHub issue #78). No exploitation reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked this run: not in CISA KEV catalog 2026.11.25.
action: Inventory services that decompress untrusted zstd input with reused contexts and update zstd (the upstream fix is in PR #5023) when your distro ships it.
product: Zstandard (zstd) 1.5.1 through 1.5.7, plus ports such as ZstdSharp

title: 13 malicious NuGet packages (fake WinUI/WPF controls) target .NET developers via fake job assessments
why: Not ahead: Socket reported 13 packages (Nov 23) and NuGet, run by Microsoft, has already removed them, including the last listed one by Nov 24.
action: Search developer machines and repos for references to the packages Socket lists and treat any machine that built such a project as compromised.
product: nuget.org packages (WinUI.Button, VS_Builder, HappyOne.* and others)
